title: Thorn and Garden Again
premise: Rafael Sterling has spent twenty years in the Hollow, a valley where magic dies at the borders, hiding the storm-calling gift that got their family exiled. When King Aldric's crown announces a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted—driven by a parasitic entity called the Verdancy that has fused itself to the royal line—refugees flood into the valley carrying seeds of the same corruption. Rafael learns the Verdancy was born from their grandmother's stolen inheritance: a garden-magic meant to heal the land, twisted by the first Sterling king into a tool of control. To end the hunt and free the king, Rafael must leave the valley that has kept them safe, reclaim an inheritance they never wanted, and choose between destroying the Verdancy—which would kill every gifted person it has rooted in—and unbinding it, which demands Rafael surrender their own storm-gift as its new anchor. In the end Rafael unbinds the crown, plants the healed garden-magic back into the land, and returns to the valley powerless but finally free.
about_author: Xanthe Fairweather is the pen name of a former botanist who traded greenhouses for grimoires after a decade cataloguing endangered plants in mountain valleys. They write fantasy about inherited burdens, quiet rebellions, and the wild things that grow in the cracks of empires.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Twenty years of careful invisibility in the Hollow are established through Rafael's daily rituals: dampening their storms, tending a neighbor's roof, never crossing the border stones. A herald's proclamation crackles from a passing airship—the crown will hunt the gifted. Emotional beat: the fragile peace shattering.

chapters.title: Refugees at the Stones
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Frightened travelers arrive at the valley's edge, some already showing green-veined skin—the mark of the Verdancy's rooting. Rafael recognizes the corruption from childhood stories and realizes the hunt is not cruelty but harvest. Emotional beat: guilt, as Rafael's safety is built on others' exposure.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with a letter from their late grandmother. The letter reveals the Sterlings once held the Gardenwright inheritance—healing magic given to the first king, who twisted it into the Verdancy to bind his heirs' power. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed from shame to responsibility.

chapters.title: The Green in the Well
chapters.summary: Maren, a refugee herbalist's POV. The Verdancy's seeds take root in the valley's water despite the border stones; magic cannot follow here, but corruption can. Maren and Rafael clash over whether to flee or fight. Emotional beat: the illusion of sanctuary collapsing.

chapters.title: Crownhunters on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Crown hunters led by Serah Vane, a disenchanted knight, breach the valley seeking the 'last storm-caller.' Rafael's suppressed gift flares involuntarily, saving refugees but revealing them. Emotional beat: terror and the strange relief of being seen.

chapters.title: Bargain with a Knight
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. Vane captures Rafael but hesitates—she has seen what the Verdancy does to captured gifted children in the capital. She offers a truce: Rafael comes willingly to the palace, or the whole valley burns. Emotional beat: moral compromise under duress.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Crossing the border stones for the first time, Rafael's storm-gift roars back like a drowned thing surfacing—overwhelming, intoxicating, dangerous. They nearly level a hillside before Vane talks them down. Emotional beat: power as both homecoming and threat.

chapters.title: The Road of Rooted Things
chapters.summary: Rafael and Vane's alternating POV. On the road to the capital they pass villages where the Verdancy has 'rooted' entire communities into placid, smiling servitude. Rafael learns the entity feeds on gifted magic specifically. Emotional beat: horror at a corruption that wears contentment's face.

chapters.title: The Gilded City
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The capital is beautiful and wrong—gardens bloom out of season, citizens move with uncanny serenity. Rafael infiltrates the palace as Vane's prisoner while secretly contacting an underground of unrooted gifted. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread beneath splendor.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. King Aldric receives them; behind his eyes flickers a terrified man drowning inside his own body. The Verdancy speaks through him, offering Rafael a place beside the throne if they stop resisting. Emotional beat: pity entangled with revulsion.

chapters.title: Cells and Seeds
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Rafael meets Wren, a child whose gift the Verdancy is slowly consuming. Through Wren, Rafael experiences the entity's memories: it was once the Gardenwright's healing spirit, starved and warped by generations of kings. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster.

chapters.title: Vane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. Ordered to root Rafael by force, Vane instead frees them, confessing her own sister was consumed years ago. Together they reach the underground, led by a root-singer named Ovid who knows the old rites. Emotional beat: betrayal transformed into alliance.

chapters.title: The Rite of Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ovid's POV. The underground explains the choice: destroy the Verdancy and every rooted person—including Wren and half the city—dies with it; or re-anchor it in a willing vessel who surrenders their own gift forever. Emotional beat: the weight of arithmetic written in lives.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Palace
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Verdancy senses the plot and roots the palace guard against them. Rafael unleashes their full storm-calling for the first time, tearing through the gilded halls. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear of their own capacity for destruction.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, dream-vision. Touching the Verdancy's heart-root, Rafael walks their grandmother's memories: the original garden, the first king's theft, the spirit's long starvation. They understand the entity is not evil but wounded. Emotional beat: grief replacing hatred.

chapters.title: The Choice of Anchors
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The rite requires a vessel strong enough to hold the Verdancy without being consumed. Rafael realizes only a storm-caller's depth can anchor it—but anchoring means giving up the gift entirely, becoming ordinary. Emotional beat: identity weighed against duty.

chapters.title: Root and Ruin
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The climax begins: Vane holds the gates, Ovid sings the binding-song, Wren resists being pulled under, and Rafael descends into the Verdancy's heart beneath the throne room. Emotional beat: desperate, coordinated sacrifice.

chapters.title: Unbinding the Crown
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Inside the entity, Rafael finds King Aldric's buried self and offers him a hand out. Together they persuade the starving spirit to release its grip—not destroyed, but returned to the land as the healing garden it was meant to be. Emotional beat: mercy as the true victory.

chapters.title: After the Storm
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. The city wakes from its placid trance; the rooted survive, freed. Aldric, diminished and human, abdicates much of his power to a council including gifted representatives. Vane chooses exile over a medal. Emotional beat: exhausted, imperfect hope.

chapters.title: Ordinary Hands
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Powerless now, Rafael struggles with the silence where the storm lived—grief for the gift that defined them. Wren, recovering, asks why Rafael gave it up. Rafael answers: because someone had to, and because they were more than the storm. Emotional beat: mourning and self-acceptance.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael returns to the Hollow carrying a cutting of the restored garden-magic, planting it beyond the border stones so the valley will no longer need to forget. Refugees begin rebuilding; Maren forgives; the valley opens its roads. Emotional beat: reconciliation with home.

chapters.title: Thorn and Garden Again
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue. Years later, Rafael teaches children—gifted and not—in the valley school, telling the story honestly, thorns included. A storm gathers on the horizon and Rafael simply watches it pass, unafraid. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity chosen rather than inherited.
